title: Schema Sampling — Core Method
description: A profiler cannot read a billion rows, so it samples: a few thousand records drawn uniformly, then field presence counted across the sample. Fields present in nearly every record are core schema; rare fields are optional or legacy. The sample size is chosen so presence estimates carry tight confidence intervals, and the sampling method is recorded with the profile. Honest sampling turns an unknowable whole into a trustworthy sketch. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Record-Type Clustering — Core Method
description: Many databases mix several record shapes — orders and customers in one store, articles and comments in another. The profiler clusters records by their field sets, and each cluster becomes a discovered record type with its own mini-schema. Simple exact-match clustering on sorted field tuples already separates clean cases; fuzzier matching handles noisy ones. Naming the clusters is left to heuristics or humans, but the separation itself is the valuable discovery. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Cardinality Estimation — Core Method
description: How many distinct values does a field hold — a handful of categories or millions of unique IDs? Cardinality estimation answers with sketches like HyperLogLog that use kilobytes to estimate billions, or exactly on samples with extrapolation. High-cardinality fields are identifiers; low-cardinality fields are categories or flags; medium ones deserve a closer look. This single measurement guides indexing decisions and join planning downstream. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Purpose Inference — Core Method
description: From structure, the profiler guesses purpose: timestamped append-only records suggest an event log; wide rows with personal fields suggest a customer master; dense inter-record references suggest a catalog. These are heuristics, scored and reported with their evidence, never asserted as fact. The inferred purpose routes the database to the right downstream handling — logs get time-series treatment, masters get entity resolution. A wrong guess is cheap because the evidence trail lets a human correct it in seconds. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Profile Reports — Core Method
description: The profile is rendered as a structured report: record types with field lists, cardinality classes, inferred purpose with evidence, and the sampling parameters behind every number. Reports are stored alongside the database and refreshed when the profiler detects schema drift. Because every claim cites its sample, the report is auditable — a skeptic can re-run the exact sampling and check. The profile becomes the database's ID card for every tool that meets it later. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
